issues.title: Sinestro, Part One
issues.summary: On Oa, the Guardians allow Sinestro to wield a Green Lantern ring again, despite Ganthet’s doubts. Meanwhile, Hal Jordan is stranded on Earth without his ring and struggles to keep his life together. After a misunderstanding involving Carol Ferris, he returns home to find an eviction notice. On Korugar, Sinestro discovers that the Sinestro Corps has enslaved the people he once ruled. He kills a disobedient Corps member and destroys the soldier’s yellow ring. Realizing his former followers have become a threat to his homeworld, Sinestro travels to Earth and finds Hal. He offers to restore Hal’s ring—but only if Hal agrees to follow his orders.

issues.title: Sinestro, Part Two
issues.summary: Sinestro offers Hal Jordan a new Green Lantern ring, but Hal attacks him as soon as he puts it on. Sinestro reveals that he can control the ring and shut it down whenever he chooses, making Hal dependent on him. When a bridge collapses in Coast City, Hal tries to save the victims, but Sinestro disables his ring to teach him a lesson. Sinestro then rescues everyone and reconstructs the bridge, demonstrating a more effective use of the ring. Their demonstration is interrupted by Gorgor, a Sinestro Corps member responsible for the disaster. Sinestro kills him and explains that his Corps has become cruel and tyrannical. He needs Hal's help to free Korugar from his own former army.

issues.title: Sinestro, Part Three
issues.summary: Hal agrees to accompany Sinestro to Korugar, though he refuses to accept Sinestro's claim of superiority. On Oa, the Guardians strip Ganthet of his emotions and discuss replacing the Green Lantern Corps with a new force. Meanwhile, Hal and Sinestro arrive on Korugar and plan to disable the Sinestro Corps' Central Power Battery. Sinestro draws the Corps members away while Hal enters the battery, but it begins to disintegrate him. As Sinestro watches in horror, the mission appears to have ended in disaster. On Earth, Carol Ferris sees news footage of Hal working alongside Sinestro and cannot believe they have become allies.

issues.title: Sinestro, Part Four
issues.summary: Hal is seemingly disintegrated inside the Sinestro Corps' Central Power Battery, while Sinestro struggles to understand what has happened. The battery's reaction to the Green Lantern energy destabilizes it, and Hal eventually emerges alive, though badly shaken. Sinestro's attempt to liberate Korugar grows more complicated as the enslaved Korugarians remain afraid of him because of his own history as their ruler. Arsona and other prisoners resist the Corps, while Sinestro confronts the consequences of the army he created. The pair must find a way to defeat the Corps and its power source before the people of Korugar can truly be free.

issues.title: Sinestro, Part Five
issues.summary: Hal and Sinestro continue their fight to free Korugar from the Sinestro Corps. The imprisoned Korugarians obtain temporary power rings and try to turn them against Sinestro, but the rings cannot harm their creator. Professor Insidd attempts to find a way to neutralize Sinestro's power battery, only for the battery to respond to Sinestro's commands and kill him. The resistance faces the danger of becoming consumed by revenge, while Sinestro must confront the consequences of the Corps' rule and his own legacy. Hal and Sinestro push toward a final confrontation with the force that has enslaved Korugar.

issues.title: The Other Hero
issues.summary: With the battle for Korugar over, Sinestro and Hal face the question of what comes next. Sinestro sends Hal back to Earth, where Hal tries to repair his damaged relationship with Carol Ferris and acknowledge the mistakes he has made. Their partnership has shown Hal a different, more ruthless kind of heroism, even as Sinestro remains a deeply troubling ally. On Oa, the Guardians pursue a far more ominous plan: they intend to unleash the First Lantern and build a Third Army to replace the Green Lantern Corps. The victory on Korugar therefore closes one conflict while setting up a much larger threat to the universe.

issues.title: The Secret of the Indigo Tribe, Part One
issues.summary:
Sinestro tries to make Hal Jordan work with him again, explaining that the Guardians intend to replace the Green Lantern Corps with a new force. Hal refuses to trust him, and their argument turns violent. When Indigo-1 and her Lanterns arrive, they seize Sinestro because they believe the Guardians made a mistake by giving him a green ring. Hal follows them to the Indigo homeworld rather than leave Sinestro in their hands.

On Oa, the Guardians interrogate Lyssa Drak about the Book of the Black and the First Lantern, revealing that they are pursuing their own secret plan. On the Indigo world, Hal wakes in a cell with his ring drained and encounters Black Hand, who has also been captured by the Tribe. Indigo-1’s intervention is not a rescue: she intends to deal with Sinestro herself.

issues.title: The Secret of the Indigo Tribe, Part Two
issues.summary:
Hal and Sinestro are trapped on the Indigo homeworld, powerless and pursued by the Indigo Tribe. Sinestro is restrained and subjected to the Tribe’s influence, while Hal tries to understand why Indigo-1 has singled out his former mentor, Abin Sur. Their escape attempt forces Hal and Sinestro to cooperate even though neither trusts the other.

The issue explains that the Indigo Lanterns’ apparent compassion has a brutal origin: their power can suppress their former personalities and force them to feel empathy. Indigo-1’s connection to Abin Sur is central to the Tribe’s creation, and the story begins to reveal how he and Natromo turned violent criminals into Indigo Lanterns.

issues.title: The Secret of the Indigo Tribe, Part Three
issues.summary:
Hal and Sinestro learn how the Indigo Tribe was created. Abin Sur and Natromo discovered the indigo light and used it to transform Iroque—a ruthless killer who would become Indigo-1—and other criminals into members of a group compelled to feel compassion. The Tribe’s benevolent appearance therefore hides a coercive form of rehabilitation: its members’ cruelty has been suppressed rather than simply overcome.

On Oa, the Guardians continue their own plan to replace the Green Lantern Corps, showing that they are willing to sacrifice their existing Lanterns to achieve it. The two storylines bring the series’ personal conflict over Sinestro together with the Guardians’ larger conspiracy.

issues.title: The Secret of the Indigo Tribe, Part Four
issues.summary:
The origin of the Indigo Tribe is fully exposed: Abin Sur and Natromo created the Tribe to use the indigo light to force dangerous criminals to experience compassion. Indigo-1 was once Iroque, a killer whose personality was changed by the ring. The revelation explains why the Tribe has such a strong interest in Sinestro, whose own history makes him a candidate for the same forced transformation.

Hal and Sinestro’s encounter with the Tribe reaches its conclusion, but their problems are far from over. The Guardians continue preparing to replace the Green Lantern Corps, and their secret plans become the next major threat to Hal, Sinestro and the other Lanterns.

issues.title: The Revenge of Black Hand, Part One
issues.summary:
The Indigo Tribe releases Sinestro from its control and places him in Hal Jordan’s custody. Natromo has reversed the connection between their rings: Hal can now control Sinestro’s ring, just as Sinestro previously controlled Hal’s. Sinestro asks what happened to Black Hand, but the pair find only black residue near a cliff and realize that Black Hand has apparently killed himself to escape being taken by the Indigo Tribe again.

Black Hand has in fact returned from the dead. On Earth, he murders the people in a restaurant, then resurrects his own dead family in a cemetery. He announces his intention to turn everyone in the world into a zombie so that he will no longer be the only person separated from the living. Meanwhile, the Guardians locate Sinestro and begin closing in on him.

issues.title: The Revenge of Black Hand, Part Two
issues.summary:
Black Hand begins carrying out his plan to spread undeath. After escaping the Indigo Tribe by dying and returning to life, he resurrects his family and sets out to turn the living into zombies. His actions are not simply an attack on Hal Jordan: he wants to remake the world so that no one will be alive in the way that once made him feel isolated.

Hal and Sinestro are forced to pursue him while dealing with their reversed ring bond, which leaves Hal able to shut down Sinestro’s power. Indigo-1 and Natromo prepare the Tribe to confront the Guardians, believing that even the Guardians can be redeemed; Sinestro rejects that faith and warns Indigo-1 not to try to force him back into the Tribe. The conflict with Black Hand escalates toward the major turning point in Green Lantern Annual #1, which concludes this storyline.

issues.title: The Revenge of Black Hand: Conclusion
issues.summary:
Hal Jordan and Sinestro dig themselves out of the grave where Black Hand left them and confront him and his army of the dead. Their power is not enough to overcome the Black Ring and the mass of resurrected corpses, and the Guardians intervene at the decisive moment.

The Guardians reveal the Chamber of Shadows, where a hidden group of Oans has kept the First Lantern imprisoned for ages. They attack their own kin, kill one of them and seize the First Lantern so they can exploit his power. The Guardians then empower Black Hand, who appears to kill Hal and Sinestro; their rings flee into the Dead Zone with them. With the First Lantern in their possession and the Corps’ greatest defenders out of the way, the Guardians begin creating the Third Army. This issue closes The Revenge of Black Hand and serves as the direct prologue to Rise of the Third Army.

issues.title: The New Normal
issues.summary:
Simon Baz becomes the newest Green Lantern, but his origin begins with him being treated as a criminal. An Arab-American mechanic with a record for stealing cars, Simon is arrested after a stolen van containing a bomb is linked to him. He insists he had no idea what was inside and is interrogated as a suspected terrorist.

While Simon is in custody, a Green Lantern ring chooses him and gives him extraordinary power. The issue follows his uneasy first steps as a Lantern: he is frightened, angry and distrustful of the authorities, while the FBI and members of the Justice League regard him as a possible threat. In parallel, Hal Jordan and Sinestro remain lost in the Dead Zone after the events of Green Lantern Annual #1. Simon’s selection introduces a new protagonist just as the Guardians’ plan to replace the Corps is about to become an open attack.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army: Actions and Reactions
issues.summary:
The Guardians begin the final stage of their plan to replace the Green Lantern Corps. Using the power extracted from the mysterious First Lantern, they unleash the first Third Army soldiers: pale, almost featureless creatures that assimilate living beings and turn them into more of their own kind. The Guardians present the project as a way to impose perfect order, but the method makes clear that their ideal universe has no room for individual will.

On Earth, Simon Baz is trying to understand the ring that has chosen him while the authorities still regard him as a criminal. His past weighs on him: he feels responsible for the accident that left his brother-in-law Nazir brain-dead and for the damage he has caused his family. His sister Sira is angry with him but agrees to meet him at their old school. Simon goes there hoping to make amends; instead, the Justice League confronts him, demanding answers about the missing Hal Jordan and treating the new Lantern as a potential threat. The issue ends with Simon facing Batman, Superman, Wonder Woman, Aquaman, Flash and Cyborg, while the Third Army has already begun tracking his ring. His new status quo is clear: Simon is Earth’s Green Lantern, but he has neither public trust nor the support of the established Corps.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
John Stewart and Guy Gardner discover that the Guardians are changing the Corps from within, even as the Third Army begins devouring worlds. In deep space, miners are attacked and assimilated by the new creatures. On Oa, the Guardians promote Guy to Lantern Sentinel in a public ceremony, apparently rewarding his service. The honour is a calculated move: the Guardians are positioning Guy where they can manipulate him and use him as an example to the Corps.

The Guardians also unleash Xar, the alien responsible for killing Green Lantern trainees, and Guy is expected to accept their version of events. Meanwhile, John learns that a new Green Lantern has appeared on Earth, while the Third Army spreads and the Corps is sent to contain it without being told what the creatures really are. Guy’s promotion temporarily raises his standing, but it also puts him directly in the Guardians’ sights. The issue’s ending establishes the central trap for the Corps: the Guardians publicly celebrate Guy while secretly preparing to destroy the people they claim to lead. The Third Army is not just an invading force; it is the Guardians’ replacement for the Green Lanterns.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Kyle Rayner’s attempt to master the emotional spectrum takes a painful turn when Atrocitus tries to teach him the meaning of rage. Kyle arrives on Earth and learns heartbreaking news, while Carol Ferris begins a new chapter as a Star Sapphire rather than simply remaining defined by her relationship with Hal Jordan. Her new ring and role broaden the uneasy alliance of Lanterns Kyle has assembled from the different Corps.

Atrocitus takes Kyle into a war zone and forces him to witness a father being murdered in front of his son. Kyle initially resists the Red Lantern power, but the scene pushes him into genuine fury; he breaks free and uses the ring’s rage to kill the men responsible. The moment proves he can access the red light, but it also shows how dangerous the process is: mastering an emotion is not the same as controlling what it makes him do. Kyle’s status quo at the end is that his training has become far more personal and brutal, while the New Guardians remain a fragile coalition whose members do not share the same methods or motives. The Third Army’s rise now threatens every colour of the spectrum, not only the Green Lanterns.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
On Arhtky, Taya tries to escape the warlord Cord after he enslaves her and her sister. When her sister is killed, Taya’s rage draws the attention of Atrocitus and the Red Lanterns. She briefly finds refuge with a couple living in the woods, but the man betrays the women to Cord for money. Cord’s men shoot them; the Red Lanterns arrive and punish the warlord and his followers.

The apparent rescue becomes a demonstration of how little the Red Lanterns understand the new threat. The Third Army attacks, and its creatures prove resistant to the corps’ usual brutal methods. Atrocitus, Bleez and Rankorr survive, but another Red Lantern is assimilated, and Taya is also transformed into one of the enemy. Atrocitus studies the attackers and notices that their eyes may be a weak point; he also realizes that the creatures share pain through a collective mind. The issue ends with the Red Lanterns badly shaken but with their first tactical lead. Their new status quo is a war on two fronts: they still seek vengeance against injustice, but now they must confront an enemy that can turn their own victims—and their own soldiers—into part of its army.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army: Courage
issues.summary:
The Justice League wants Simon Baz to explain himself—and to account for Hal Jordan’s disappearance. Simon’s attempt to establish himself as a Green Lantern is interrupted by Batman, Superman, Wonder Woman, Aquaman, Flash and Cyborg. They do not know whether to trust him, and Simon’s defensiveness only makes the encounter more volatile. He is a new hero with a criminal record, a family in crisis and no mentor to explain what the ring expects of him.

At the same time, the Guardians continue to conceal their plan from the Corps. The Lanterns discover disturbing evidence that the Guardians are not merely responding to the crisis but are responsible for the Third Army and its spread. The creatures assimilate living beings, turning every encounter into a potential multiplication of the enemy. The issue closes with Simon still under suspicion and the Corps beginning to recognize that its leaders may be lying to it. The status quo shifts on both fronts: Simon has to prove himself without institutional support, while the Green Lanterns are approaching a crisis of faith in the Guardians who created them.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Guy Gardner leads his squad against the Third Army near Saturn, where the Lanterns are overwhelmed by creatures that assimilate their victims. Vandor is lost to the enemy, and the squad’s resistance collapses as the Third Army strips Lanterns of their rings and absorbs them. Guy manages to escape, but the Guardians have been watching the battle and use the disaster to discredit him.

The attack is part of a larger plan. Xar is sent toward Earth to threaten Guy’s family, while Kilowog and Salaak investigate why fewer power rings are reaching new recruits. They discover that the Guardians have blocked rings from leaving Oa. Salaak also reveals that the Guardians supplied the misleading footage used to implicate John Stewart in the death of Krrt. Guy returns to Oa expecting to explain himself, but the Guardians publicly blame him for the deaths of his squad and a peace delegation, accuse him of disobedience, and demand that he resign. He does so and is expelled from the Corps. The issue ends with Guy back on Earth without his ring or rank, while the Guardians turn him into a scapegoat and continue their purge. His new status quo is that he must protect his family and act as a hero without being a Green Lantern.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Kyle continues his emotional-spectrum training with Indigo-1, concentrating on compassion. Their discussion challenges Kyle’s assumption that compassion is simply a benevolent feeling: the Indigo light can channel other emotions, and using it requires understanding rather than suppressing what he feels. Kyle is still learning how to move between the colours without being overwhelmed by them.

Arkillo attacks, testing Kyle’s ability to face fear rather than run from it. Kyle manages to turn that fear back against Arkillo and survive the confrontation. Carol Ferris arrives, and her presence raises questions about her devotion to Hal Jordan, who remains missing. She and Kyle set off to find Larfleeze, hoping the Orange Lantern may help them locate Hal. Arkillo follows, partly because finding Hal may lead him to Sinestro, whom he still wants to challenge. The issue ends with Kyle, Carol and Arkillo travelling together despite their incompatible loyalties. The team’s status quo has shifted again: the New Guardians are becoming a more practical alliance, built around the search for Hal and the need to master every colour before the Third Army overwhelms them.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Atrocitus and the Red Lanterns return to Arhtky to fight the Third Army, armed with a crucial discovery from the previous issue. They target the creatures’ eyes, a vulnerable point that allows the Red Lanterns to inflict real damage instead of simply watching their attacks fail. The strategy briefly turns the battle in their favour.

Rankorr, however, struggles with the act of killing. Because Taya’s consciousness seems to linger inside the Third Army creature she became, he cannot treat every enemy as an empty monster. His hesitation complicates the Red Lanterns’ assault and exposes the moral cost of their usual approach. At the same time, the conflict leads Atrocitus back toward the buried history of Ryutt, his homeworld, and the origins of his rage. The issue ends with the Red Lanterns possessing a workable tactic but no easy victory: they can damage the Third Army, yet every assimilated victim raises the question of whether there is anything left to save. Their status quo is now a more complicated war, in which rage is a weapon but not always a sufficient answer.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Back on Earth, Guy Gardner tries to rebuild his life after the Guardians force him out of the Corps. Without his ring, he still wants to help people, but his temper and reputation make it difficult to distinguish heroism from recklessness. His family becomes a key part of the story: Guy’s father and siblings are worried about him, and his sister’s police work puts them in an awkward position when Guy interferes with an operation.

On Oa, John Stewart and Salaak continue to piece together the Guardians’ deception. The Third Army is being used as a public demonstration that the Green Lantern Corps has become unnecessary, while the Guardians suppress evidence and punish anyone who questions them. The issue’s ending leaves Guy in a precarious civilian life, trying to protect his family without the ring that has defined him, while John and Salaak understand more clearly that the Guardians are deliberately undermining the Corps. The new status quo is not a simple rebellion yet: the Lanterns are scattered, Guy is powerless and disgraced, and the Guardians still control Oa—but their lies are becoming harder to contain.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Kyle Rayner turns to Larfleeze for help mastering the orange light of avarice. The Orange Lantern agrees only because Kyle has made a bargain with him; Larfleeze is incapable of sharing power without expecting something in return. When the Third Army attacks, however, the threat is so great that Larfleeze does the unthinkable and helps Kyle attempt to wield the orange energy rather than hoarding it for himself.

The lesson is as much about character as power. Kyle has to accept the selfishness and possessiveness associated with the orange light without allowing it to consume him. The Third Army’s assault interrupts the training and forces the unlikely pair to cooperate under pressure. The issue ends with Kyle still owing Larfleeze for the help and with no guarantee that he can safely master the colour; the bargain remains a real liability for the New Guardians. The status quo is that Kyle is closer to understanding the full spectrum, but every new colour comes with a personal trial—and Larfleeze’s assistance is never free.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Atrocitus discovers that the Third Army’s origins are tied to an older enemy: the Manhunters. The sight of the robotic enforcers reopens the oldest wound in his history, since the Manhunters’ massacre of his people helped create the rage that defines him. Rather than treating the Third Army as an isolated invasion, Atrocitus begins to connect it to the Guardians’ long history of imposing order through violence.

Meanwhile, Rankorr is forced to confront the consequences of his own rage. The power that made him a Red Lantern gives him the ability to strike back, but it also threatens to turn him into the kind of executioner he despises. The conflict leaves Atrocitus more determined to oppose the Guardians and less willing to trust the systems they created. By the end, the Red Lanterns’ fight has become both a tactical war against the Third Army and a personal reckoning with the Manhunters and the Guardians behind them. Their status quo is a reluctant shift from indiscriminate vengeance toward a more focused campaign against the source of their suffering.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army: Innocent Lives
issues.summary:
Simon Baz and Guy Gardner finally cross paths as the Third Army’s invasion escalates. Simon is still being treated as a suspect by the authorities and by the Justice League, while Guy has been stripped of his ring and expelled from the Corps by the Guardians. Each man has a reason to distrust the institutions that should have supported him, but each is also trying to protect people who cannot defend themselves against the growing threat.

Elsewhere, Hal Jordan and Sinestro remain trapped in the Dead Zone, and the Guardians’ Third Army continues assimilating living beings. Simon’s encounter with Guy offers the possibility of guidance from an experienced Lantern, but it is also dangerous: Guy is now a target, and Simon’s connection to the ring makes him a target too. The issue ends with the two Earth Lanterns’ paths converging just as the Third Army closes in, setting up a partnership that neither the Guardians nor the public would have expected. Simon’s status quo changes from isolated newcomer to a Lantern who may have to rely on a disgraced predecessor, while Guy must decide whether the Corps’ oath matters more than the corrupt leaders who expelled him.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
John Stewart and Fatality investigate the shattered remains of Mogo while the Guardians intensify their attack on the Corps. On Oa, the Guardians unleash horror inside the very institution they control. John and Fatality are forced to fight the Third Army while realizing that the Guardians are deliberately destroying the Corps’ ability to recruit and defend the universe.

On Earth, Guy Gardner is in jail after losing his ring and rank. Simon Baz and the small alien Lantern B’dg help him break out, and Guy immediately turns his escape into a rescue mission: he uses his knowledge of Baltimore to get his family and other civilians out of danger. Simon’s own desperate actions—including stealing military aircraft—show how far he is willing to go to protect people despite being treated as a criminal. The issue ends with Guy back in action without a ring, Simon becoming an unexpected ally, and the two trying to protect Guy’s family from the Guardians’ agents. The status quo is a divided Corps: John is fighting the enemy in space, while Guy and Simon are forming a grassroots defence on Earth.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Kyle Rayner’s training brings him closer to mastering the full emotional spectrum. The lessons of compassion, fear and avarice have taught him that every colour demands a different kind of self-knowledge, and the New Guardians’ uneasy cooperation is the only way he can continue. The Third Army attacks before Kyle’s mastery is secure, forcing him to use what he has learned under real pressure.

The crisis pushes Kyle toward a new role: he is no longer simply a Green Lantern carrying several rings, but the one person capable of bringing the spectrum together. Ganthet’s guidance and the memories of Kyle’s past make clear that emotional connection—not domination—is the missing element in the Guardians’ attempt to create perfect order. The issue closes with Kyle’s mastery still developing, but with the path toward the White Lantern power now visible. His status quo changes from student to the New Guardians’ essential weapon against the Third Army, setting up the next phase of the crossover and the conflict over the First Lantern.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Atrocitus faces an impossible choice when the Red Lanterns’ battle brings them into contact with the Manhunters and the history of the Five Inversions. The Manhunters are confused and leaderless, but they are also instruments of the Guardians’ old campaign of annihilation. Atrocitus has every reason to destroy them; their crimes helped make him what he is. Yet he recognizes that the Guardians’ current plan threatens to repeat the same cycle on a universal scale.

Instead of simply tearing the Manhunters apart, Atrocitus proposes that they work together against the greater threat. It is a startling reversal for a character whose identity is built on vengeance, and it does not mean he has forgiven the machines or abandoned his rage. It means he has found a target more urgent than his old enemies. The issue ends with a fragile, deeply mistrustful alliance between the Red Lanterns and the Manhunters. Their status quo is transformed: Atrocitus has begun turning his rage into strategy, and the Red Lanterns now have potential allies in the fight against the Guardians and the Third Army.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army: Trial by Fire
issues.summary:
Simon Baz’s story converges with the wider Corps crisis as he finally encounters Guy Gardner. Simon has been struggling to prove that the ring chose him for a reason; Guy has been expelled and publicly blamed for the failures the Guardians engineered. Their meeting creates an uneasy connection between the new Lantern and the veteran who has just lost everything that made him a Lantern in the eyes of the Corps.

On Oa, the Guardians’ plan reaches a terrifying stage. The Third Army is spreading, the Corps is being weakened from within, and the Guardians continue exploiting the power of the First Lantern to carry out their design. The story also returns to Hal Jordan and Sinestro in the Dead Zone, where their survival and escape remain tied to the crisis. The issue ends with the Guardians’ control approaching its breaking point, but not before the Corps is pushed toward collapse. Simon’s new status quo is that he is no longer simply an isolated newcomer: he is becoming part of the resistance to the Guardians, and the story now points directly toward the final confrontation and the next event, Wrath of the First Lantern.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army: Finale
issues.summary:
The Guardians’ plan reaches its apparent triumph: the Third Army has devastated the Corps, and the Guardians shut down the Green Lanterns they created. Guy Gardner and Simon Baz find themselves among the few Lanterns still able to act freely. Guy has been stripped of his ring and rank, but his will to protect others remains; Simon, the new Lantern of Earth, is no longer simply trying to clear his name and prove himself. Their unexpected alliance becomes central to the final confrontation on Oa.

The surviving Lanterns launch a desperate attack against the Guardians and the Third Army. The Guardians believe that obedience and forced uniformity will make the universe safe, but the Lanterns’ resistance exposes the fatal flaw in that vision: the Guardians cannot control every act of courage or every choice made by those they have cast aside. The Third Army crisis reaches its conclusion, but the victory does not restore the old order. The Guardians’ actions have unleashed a much more dangerous mystery connected to the First Lantern, and the story points directly into Wrath of the First Lantern. The new status quo is a shattered Corps, a discredited leadership and a looming threat beyond the Third Army itself.
